findings.title: No duplicate $149 charge on INV-2609
findings.explanation: TX-9002 was an authorization at 10:02:11 UTC that hit a capture_timeout; the system retried and created TX-9001 at 10:02:49 UTC, which was captured/settled. TX-9002 was never captured and was released on 2026-09-18 (capture_status: not_captured, released_at set, linked_payment_id cross-references TX-9001). Only one $149 payment actually settled against INV-2609. This matches normal authorization/retry behavior under POL-B-AUTH, not a duplicate charge.

findings.title: SUP-5601 agent improperly promised a refund pre-review
findings.explanation: Agent S-22 concluded 'duplicate charge' from viewing two payment rows without checking capture status, and told the customer a $149 refund would be processed within 5-7 business days. POL-B-REF requires billing-specialist approval before any refund is promised; support agents may not commit to refunds pre-review. This commitment was made without review and is not supported by the underlying facts (no duplicate charge exists). SUP-5602 correctly paused the refund pending investigation.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics $30 add-on is a legitimate, authorized charge
findings.explanation: Subscription event SE-6 shows admin seat U-2 added the deep_time_monthly add-on on 2026-09-12, set to start at the next renewal (2026-09-14). This matches POL-B-ADD (owner or any admin seat may add add-ons; mid-cycle additions start next renewal and are invoiced separately at full monthly price). The $30 charge on INV-2609-AO / TX-9003 aligns exactly with this add and the renewal date. Not unauthorized.

findings.title: July plan upgrade and proration credit were calculated correctly
findings.explanation: On 2026-07-02 the owner upgraded shelf_monthly to vault_monthly. INV-2607P charged $59.60 for the prorated new-plan cost (12 of 30 remaining days), and CR-778 ($19.60) was issued for unused time on the old plan, consistent with POL-B-PRO. The math and process for the upgrade itself were correct.

findings.title: Unapplied credit CR-778 was never flagged to the owner as required
findings.explanation: Auto-apply for credits was disabled on 2026-05-02 (SE-4, ref SUP-5390). CR-778 ($19.60), issued 2026-07-02, remains unapplied with owner_notified=false. It is now well over 30 days old. POL-B-CRD requires that with auto-apply disabled, unapplied credits older than 30 days must be flagged to the account owner (owner_notified=true) and then applied or refunded per the owner's instruction. This flagging never happened — a genuine process compliance gap independent of the refund dispute.

corrections.prior_claim: Two $149 payments for INV-2609 indicate a duplicate charge, and a $149 refund would be processed within 5-7 business days.
corrections.corrected_claim: Only one $149 payment (TX-9001) was actually captured/settled for INV-2609. The second record (TX-9002) was an authorization that timed out and was released, never captured. There is no duplicate charge and no refund is owed on this basis.

unresolved_questions: Should CR-778 ($19.60) now be applied to the customer's current/next invoice or refunded, per the owner's instruction, once notified as required by POL-B-CRD?
Does the customer need formal outreach retracting the S-22 refund promise from SUP-5601, given no duplicate charge was found?

actions_requiring_human_authorization.description: Notify account owner of the U-1/C-1042 account about unapplied credit CR-778 ($19.60, issued 2026-07-02 for unused time on prior plan) since auto-apply is disabled and the credit is over 30 days old, per POL-B-CRD, and ask whether to apply it to an invoice or refund it.
Apply CR-778 ($19.60) to an outstanding/upcoming invoice for C-1042, pending owner's instruction after notification.
Formally withdraw/correct the $149 refund commitment made by agent S-22 in SUP-5601, since investigation shows no duplicate charge occurred; communicate this finding to the customer.
